description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000) on the x-axis. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 60% to 80%. The Base method is shown as a black line with circle markers, starting at approximately 60.5% and increasing to about 66% over the range. The MEND method, represented by a brown line with diamond markers, begins near 66% and rises to about 74%. The FT method, shown as a blue line with triangle markers, starts around 62% and increases to approximately 68%. The MEMIT method, depicted as a purple line with star markers, begins near 65% and rises to about 72%. The IKE method, shown as a red line with triangle markers, starts at approximately 65% and ends near 70%. The ROME method, represented by a green line with square markers, begins at about 72% and rises to approximately 77%, before leveling off slightly near the end of the x-axis range.
